newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes weaker after quiet April expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes weaker after quiet April expiry.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended weaker on Thursday and towards the bottom of the day's range after the April contract expired with a whimper, dealers said.
May gas oil, which became the prompt contact after April expired at midday, closed $3.75 lower at $160.50 a tonne, just 75 cents off the session low.
Deliveries against the April contract, which expired at $160.25 a tonne, would total 1,072 lots, or 107,200 tonnes, an IPE official said.
"It expired very quietly. Most brokers knew both sides of the market...so it went quietly and fairly dull," said a broker.

Dealers said slack demand for heating oil in Europe, much of which is basking in abnormally high temperatures, was keeping up the pressure on IPE gas oil. Only robust Asian demand was providing sellers with a crumb of comfort, traders said.
Meanwhile, May Brent crude futures steadied after dipping to a new nine-month low of $17.54 a barrel in mid-afternoon dealing.

May Brent traded just two cents lower at $17.73 a barrel by 1713 GMT, almost exactly in the middle of the session's 33-cent range, but some brokers saw little prospect of any gains given a weak technical and fundamental picture.
"There is still quite a bit of crude in the market but a lot of weakness now is coming from the technical perspective," said a broker.
May Brent slid after breaking key support at $17.65, the previous lowest point of this year's down move posted on April 4. New support was seen at $17.52 a barrel.

Dealers said a weak opening on NYMEX crude and gasoline and the failure of May Brent to break back above technical resistance at $18.40-$18.50 in the last three trading sessions had set the scene for further losses.
